title: Gangu Shah’s Boon, Self-Exaltation, and Blackened Face

blocks.text: Guru Amar Das grants Gangu Shah a dangerous boon by allowing his words to carry worldly force, and that gift soon becomes the basis for wider influence in the hills. Instead of remaining a servant, he moves toward self-exaltation and begins acting like a guru in his own right.

His failure becomes unmistakable when he neglects proper obedience around Bibi Bhani's wedding and places his own importance ahead of the Guru's order. The rebuke is severe and memorable because his face had turned blackish, giving visible form to the inward stain of arrogance.
The page therefore marks both empowerment and judgment. Gangu Shah receives extraordinary effectiveness, but the same story shows how quickly a boon curdles when it is used to magnify the self.
